PluginConfig:
Network Scanner — discovers LAN devices via passive traffic sniffing, ARP sweep, ping and TCP probe. Creates one Indigo device per MAC address; tracks online/offline state, IP, vendor and open ports.

── Experts only ─────────────────────
Show experts section
Defaults here are the measured best choice for a normal LAN. Change them only to work around a specific problem, and measure before and after.
Enable ARP Sweep
Sweep the subnet with ARP requests to discover new devices.
Enable Passive Traffic Sniffing
Passively capture all ethernet traffic via tcpdump to detect any active device — not just ARP. Catches devices that suppress ARP responses. Each MAC is throttled to one update per 5 s. Requires sudo password below if tcpdump does not already have the BPF entitlement.
Enable Active mDNS Query
on off auto (alternate 2 sweeps on / 2 off, and keep score)
Sends one mDNS PTR query at the start of each ARP sweep — a single 50-byte multicast packet — prompting mDNS-capable devices to announce themselves. Finds devices hidden behind proxy-ARP access points (HomePod, Sonos, AirPort Express); responses are picked up by the passive sniff thread. "auto" by default: repeated A/B runs could not separate on from off — each landed inside its own noise — so auto settles it over days of normal use instead. The one report of trouble attributed to this query turned out to be the plugin timeout bug, fixed separately. Use "Test mDNS Query On/Off" in the plugin menu to measure both ways on your own network before changing this. "auto" alternates 2 sweeps on, 2 sweeps off, for ever, and accumulates the sighting totals for each - print them with "Print mDNS auto totals". Short A/B runs all landed inside their own noise here, so auto is the way to get an answer over days rather than minutes.
Resolve host names in arp
OFF (the default) runs arp -an and reads the cache numerically. ON runs arp -a , which does one reverse-DNS lookup per cache entry, so the run time scales with the size of the ARP cache rather than your network: on a host whose cache had filled with ~1500 proxy-ARP'd 169.254.x.x entries from a single device, arp -a took over two hours while arp -an took 0.04 s. That is what trips the arp timeout every cycle and logs a warning. The host name from arp is only a fallback — mDNS/Bonjour names take priority and are unaffected by this setting.
Create Synthetic Devices for Ping-Only Hosts
If an IP responds to ping but never appears in ARP (e.g. a device on a different VLAN), create an Indigo device for it using a synthetic MAC address (00:00:00:00:00:XX) and set it to ping-only mode. WARNING: some routers (proxy-ARP) answer ping on behalf of every IP on the subnet, which will flood this plugin with fake devices. Leave OFF unless you specifically need cross-VLAN monitoring.
Scan Interval
30 seconds 60 seconds 90 seconds 120 seconds
How often to run the reachability probe (ping + curl TCP fallback) on known devices. Can be tuned per device in device edit.
── Logging ──────────────────────────
Show debug section
Most logging goes to the file: ... /Perceptive Automation/Indigo xx.y/Logs/com.karlwachs.networkscanner/plugin.log
Device tracking and per-device log controls are in the Plugin Menu → Track Device / Logging Tools.
Log New Device Created
Log when a new Indigo device is created for a discovered MAC.
Log Ignored MACs Skipped
Log each time an ignored MAC is seen and skipped.
Log Online / Offline Changes
Log when a device changes between online and offline.
Log IP Address Changes
Log when a device is seen with a different IP than before.
Log Every Device Seen
Log every ARP packet or sweep hit (can be noisy).
Log ARP Sweep Activity
Log when each ARP sweep starts and finishes.
Log Ping / Probe Results
Log every ICMP ping and TCP socket probe result to plugin.log (can be noisy during sweeps).
Log Tcpdump ARP Replies
Log every ARP reply captured by tcpdump (passive sniff), including throttled ones. Very noisy on busy networks — use for proxy-ARP / IP-churn diagnosis.
Log ARP Sweep Entries (arp -a)
Log every entry parsed from arp -a during each sweep cycle, with replied/cache-only status. Use to diagnose proxy-ARP deduplication.
Log Delayed Actions
Log every queued and applied delayed action (queue time, device, states written). Use to diagnose timed state writes such as the 5 s participantsChanged reset.
